title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted
statement:
`arr` has length `n` and holds each integer from `0` to `n - 1` exactly once. Cut `arr` into consecutive, non-empty pieces ("chunks"), sort every chunk on its own, and glue the chunks back together in their original order. The cut is valid when the glued result is `[0, 1, ..., n - 1]`.

Return the maximum number of chunks a valid cut can have.
constraints: All values in arr are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of cut positions works for `n <= 10` (at most 512 cuts), but there is a direct rule. A chunk that ends at index `i` can be closed only if, after sorting, positions `0..i` hold exactly the values `0..i`. Since the values are distinct and come from `0..n-1`, that happens exactly when the largest value among `arr[0..i]` equals `i`. Cutting at every such index is always allowed and gives the most chunks.

## Approach

1. Keep `maxSeen`, the largest value in the prefix so far, starting at `-1`, and a counter `chunks`.
2. For each index `i`, update `maxSeen` with `arr[i]`.
3. If `maxSeen === i`, the prefix is exactly `{0, ..., i}`, so a chunk can end here: add one to `chunks`.
4. Return `chunks`. The last index always qualifies, so the answer is at least 1.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [4,3,2,1,0]`. At `i = 0`, `maxSeen = 4`, not 0. It stays 4 at `i = 1, 2, 3`, never equal to `i`. At `i = 4`, `maxSeen = 4 = i`, so `chunks = 1`. The whole array must be one chunk, and the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per element.
- Space: O(1): two counters.

## Pitfalls

- Comparing `arr[i]` itself with `i` is not enough: on `[0,2,1,3]` it misses the cut after index 2 and returns 2 instead of 3. The running maximum is what matters.
- Cutting wherever the next value is larger does not work either: in `[1,2,0]` the `0` at the end still belongs with the first two values.
- The rule relies on `arr` being a permutation of `0..n-1`; with repeated or arbitrary values (problem 768) a different method is needed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `chunks` | number of chunk boundaries found so far |
| `maxSeen` | largest value in `arr[0..i]` |
| `i` | current index, the candidate end of a chunk |

narration.2: No chunk has been closed yet.
narration.3: Start below every value so the first element becomes the maximum.
narration.4: Visit every index as a possible end of a chunk.
narration.5: Track the largest value seen in the prefix arr[0..i].
narration.6: If that maximum equals i, the prefix holds exactly the values 0 to i.
narration.7: So a chunk can end here: count it.
narration.10: Every index where the prefix was complete became a cut, which is the most possible.
